description: A line added to every passenger briefing that hints at what sort of passenger it is. The client says it, about {target}.

respectable: {target} is a plain traveller with plain luggage. You'll barely know they're aboard.
{target} has their papers in order, and a spare copy, and a copy of the spare.
{target} travels like this every month. They'll want a quiet berth and a hot drink.
{target} is visiting family. They've packed a present for every one of them.
{target} is going to {destination} for work. Nothing more to it.
{target} has booked a return passage already. That's the sort of passenger they are.
shady: {target} will pay the rest in cash, on arrival, and would rather you didn't ask for a name on the manifest.
{target} has no luggage to speak of, and asked twice which route avoids the patrols.
{target} would like to board after the dock shift changes. Don't ask why.
{target} gave a different name at the desk. It's probably fine.
{target} will want to know who's on the comms before you answer any hail.
{target} has paid well over the usual fare. That usually means something.
dodgy: {target} wants to leave now, before anyone comes looking. And someone will come looking.
{target} is in trouble and you'll be in it too, for a while. That's what the pay is for.
{target} is the sort of passenger who gets a ship stopped. Be ready.
shady-wanted: {target} keeps an eye on every customs boat in the dock.
{target} asked whether you'd ever been searched at {destination}.
dodgy-wanted: {target} is wanted. I won't pretend otherwise. Keep them away from customs scanners.
There's a warrant out for {target}. If a patrol asks, you've never heard of them.
shady-bounty: {target} flinches whenever a bounty board lights up.
{target} asked if you know any hunters by name. They seemed relieved when you didn't.
dodgy-bounty: There's a price on {target}, and hunters who'd like it. Don't stop for anyone.
{target} is worth more to some people than this job pays you. Remember who's paying you.
shady-debtor: {target} paid the fare in small, mismatched coins and wouldn't look at the lenders' offices.
{target} gets very quiet when anyone mentions money.
dodgy-debtor: {target} owes money to the kind of people who send ships to collect it.
{target}'s creditors are looking for them. They'll be looking at you as well.
shady-witness: {target} saw something they shouldn't have, I think. They haven't said what.
{target} keeps a sealed file close and won't let it out of reach.
dodgy-witness: {target} is going to testify, if they get there. Some people would rather they didn't.
{target} saw what happened, and the people who did it know. Get them there alive.
shady-runaway: {target} left somewhere in a hurry and doesn't want to talk about it.
{target} keeps looking at the gate charts like they're counting the distance from somewhere.
dodgy-runaway: {target} has run from people who want them back very much. They won't stop at asking.
{target} walked out on a vow. The people they made it to have ships.
shady-valuables: {target} won't let their case out of sight, not even to eat.
{target}'s luggage is very small and very heavy.
dodgy-valuables: {target} is carrying something worth a great deal, and too many people know it.
Half the bar knows what's in {target}'s bag. That's the trouble with bars.
